technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment as backward-compatible extensions to the existing Spring-based application and configuration model rather than introducing a new configuration framework.
Represent CodeGen Options and Merge Options as validated, externally configurable properties that are propagated to the relevant job and processor components.

Implement job timeout using configurable duration handling with cooperative cancellation and interruption of the executing task; document that non-interruptible external operations may not terminate immediately.

Execute SQL statements and scripts through reusable processor and job-step components backed by the existing JDBC infrastructure, with transaction behavior controlled by the surrounding job configuration.
Add dependency injection support for a user-provided RowMapper<Tuple>, retaining the current default mapper when no custom mapper is configured.
Use Spring expression evaluation for dynamic directory and file names, with a defined evaluation context containing job parameters and intermediate data available at the point of evaluation.
Implement configurable delimiter escaping in the delimited output path, preserving existing behavior by default and adding coverage for Hive/HAWQ-compatible CSV output.
Refactor MessageBus message transformation to reduce unnecessary object creation and copying while preserving message ordering, error handling, and externally observable behavior.
Use unit tests for component behavior and integration tests for representative end-to-end job configurations, including backward-compatibility coverage.
assumptions: The existing codebase, build, CI pipeline, job model, JDBC support, MessageBus implementation, and test harness are available and buildable before work starts.
The increment includes all eight user stories, but does not require changes to Spring Framework itself or to external databases, HDFS, Hive, or HAWQ products.
Existing configuration conventions and serialization formats can be extended without a breaking migration; new options have sensible defaults matching current behavior.
SQL execution is limited to the existing JDBC-supported databases and does not require vendor-specific SQL parsing or advanced script-language features.
Timeout support applies to framework-managed job or processor execution and does not guarantee termination of database calls that ignore interruption or socket timeouts.
Custom RowMapper<Tuple> implementations are supplied through the existing dependency-injection/configuration mechanism and do not require a new plugin distribution system.
Expression support is limited to the expression language already used by the application, assumed to be Spring Expression Language or an equivalent existing evaluator.
Delimiter escaping follows standard configurable CSV-style quoting or escaping rules and does not require support for every possible serialization format.
MessageBus performance work is an internal refactor with no intentional public API change.
One developer performs implementation, testing, documentation, code review preparation, and integration work; estimates are work-hours and exclude elapsed scheduling time.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing job, processor, configuration, JDBC, output, and MessageBus implementations; identify extension points; define option defaults, compatibility behavior, validation rules, and test scope for all eight stories.
Add configuration properties and propagation for CodeGen Options, implement validation and default handling, connect the options to code generation execution, and add focused tests.

Expose Merge Options through the supported configuration model, pass them through the merge and megastore-related execution path, preserve existing defaults, and test incremental delta consumption scenarios.

Add timeout configuration, validation, scheduling and cancellation behavior for managed jobs or processors, define timeout error reporting, and test completion, timeout, cancellation, and default behavior.

activities.activity_name: Add SQL statement and script execution
activities.activity_description: Implement reusable SQL execution support usable from a processor or job statement, including statement/script handling, parameter integration, transaction/error behavior, configuration wiring, and JDBC integration tests.

Add injection and lifecycle support for a user-provided RowMapper<Tuple>, retain the default mapper, integrate it with JDBC item-reader creation, and test enrichment of tuples without processor-side reconstruction.

activities.activity_name: Add expression-based directory and file naming
activities.activity_description: Integrate expression evaluation into directory and file name resolution, expose the required job and intermediate-data context, handle evaluation errors, preserve literal names, and add dynamic-name tests.

activities.activity_name: Implement delimiter escaping for delimited output
activities.activity_description: Add configurable escaping or quoting of delimiter characters and related special characters in output records, preserve current defaults, and test CSV output containing delimiters, quotes, and line breaks.

Redesign the internal transformation path to reduce allocations and avoid unnecessary message copying, preserve transformation semantics and error handling, and add focused throughput and behavioral regression tests.

Create and execute comprehensive tests covering configuration binding, defaults, invalid inputs, end-to-end job execution, JDBC behavior, output compatibility, timeout behavior, and interactions among the new features.
Document all new options, defaults, examples, extension points, timeout limitations, SQL usage, custom RowMapper registration, expression syntax, and delimiter escaping behavior.

activities.activity_name: Final integration, review, and regression resolution
activities.activity_description: Run the complete build and regression suite, inspect compatibility and performance results, resolve defects found during integration, update release notes or migration guidance, and prepare the increment for delivery.
